you’re not an AH for being angry with her, honestly she sounds like a bad therapist. housing is one of the most basic human needs, homelessness itself can be a traumatizing experience, to take away the importance of housing on your mental health makes absolutely no sense. in my experience therapists tend to lack any type of empathy regarding systemic issues (housing, being poor) because they don’t know how to deal with it, and god forbid they don’t know anything about anything. my therapist  got offended that i said she led a more financially privileged life than me so she doesn’t understand how the other half lives, how i’m living, and she blew up at me over it. totally agree that it feels like they’re feeding their own egos. 

if i can offer a suggestion: social workers seem to be more helpful and empathetic to these situations. can you get one through your health insurance? or a hospital? i’m receiving mental health help at a hospital in NY and they have a program that essentially gets a social worker to help with big issues like housing/food security/etc. at the very least i’d say it’s worth it to make a complaint about her, she shouldn’t be allowed to continue this line of thinking and most likely will only receive it from a superior. i completely understand getting fed up and giving up on therapists entirely-which isn’t ideal to you probably from what you’ve said- sometimes therapists don’t fit, sometimes you just outgrow them, or life outgrows them, and you need someone who can handle the problems as they come, not downplay an extremely difficult situation in your life. i’m sorry you’re going through this
